text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P0 - Customer 'Stormhaven' (private VPC) reporting elevated 5xx through NLB/ALB. >30% requests failing, started ~09:12 UTC. Affected: app-prod in us-west-2 dedicated pool. Pager -> @maria oncall. Runbook: /runbooks/vpc-egress-networking

maria: I'm on it. assigning net-eng and prodeng. first pass: can people confirm whether it's ALB healthchecks failing or backend 502s?

raj: checking logs from the app nodes now. seeing a spike in connection resets to the backend service (upstream:10.4.2.0/24). also seeing increased SYN_RECV on the NLB targets.

luca: I can confirm ALB target group shows a bunch of 502/503s. NLB target reports OK but client->nlb shows TCP rst spikes. looks like intermittent conntrack / ephemeral port exhaustion on the tenant NAT gateway.

kai: adding networking notes — Stormhaven uses a shared NAT instance with conntrack table tuned conservative. I can run conntrack -L but need a jump host.

maria: quick question — are DNS lookups failing for the ALB hostname? any NXDOMAIN?

raj: ran dig; DNS is fine. nslookup app.prod.stormhaven.internal -> 10.4.2.12,13. response times normal. problem looks TCP-level.

oncall-bot: @maria reminder: escalate to SRE lead after 10m if not mitigated.

luca: hypothesis: an upstream client/tenant is opening many short-lived connections causing conntrack entries to fill then O(1) drops. I can temporarily shift egress for Stormhaven app-subnet to alternate NAT (nat-standby) to relieve the table. That will require an SG/path tweak + route table change.

kai: I can push the route change. plan: 1) add route in rt-0a1b2c to nat-standby (10.6.0.5) 2) modify security group storm-prod-sg to allow healthcheck IPs from 10.6.0.0/24 3) weight ALB->NLB failover: move 80% traffic to NLB path while we monitor.

elaine: preparing customer-facing blurb for Stormhaven support. will post once we have a concrete mitigation.

maria: do the route switch but keep a rollback plan. luca, are there any cache/KV impacts for pinned sessions?

luca: minimal. session stickiness is by cookie at the ALB layer; moving NAT does not change that. but if we redirect traffic to NLB for a subset, sticky sessions might break — we'll route by weight not full cutover.

kai: executing step 1 -> applying route change now.

[system message] deploy-bot: route-table rt-0a1b2c updated: 10.4.0.0/16 -> nat-standby (10.6.0.5) by kai at 09:22 UTC

kai: updating storm-prod-sg to allow healthcheck cidr, applying rule id sg-rule-775.

[system message] security-bot: security group storm-prod-sg modified (added inbound 10.6.0.0/24:tcp/80) by kai

maria: switching ALB weight — start 20% traffic to NLB, 80% to ALB -> increase to 50%/50% if metrics improve.

luca: running quick traffic reweight via traffic-controller.

[system message] traffic-controller: reroute initiated: ALB weight -> 60%, NLB -> 40% (operator=luca)

raj: metrics after reroute: errors down from 32% -> 12% in 2 minutes. connection resets decreased. conntrack entries for the tenant dropped from 98% to 40% used.

maria: good. continue ramp to 80% NLB over next 10 minutes if stable. can we confirm no DNS TTL weirdness?

raj: DNS TTL is low (30s) for the service, so no sticky caching problem.

kai: starting gradual increase to 80% NLB.

[system message] traffic-controller: ALB -> 20%, NLB -> 80% (operator=kai)

raj: errors down to 2.1% now. latency stable. conntrack usage steady ~12%. looks like mitigation effective.

maria: excellent. immediate next steps: 1) keep NLB at 80% for 30m monitoring window, 2) schedule a medium-term fix: increase conntrack hashsize + tune timeout for Stormhaven tenant, or provision dedicated NAT per-tenant. 3) create follow-up ticket for postmortem and customer RCA. anyone take ownership of the medium-term?

luca: I will own the medium-term (provisioning dedicated NAT or adding dedicated egress pool). I'll open a ticket with perf numbers and expected rollout plan.

kai: I'll capture the exact SG & route diffs and commit them to infra-ops change set.

elaine: here's a draft status update to send to Stormhaven support — please edit: 

"Hi Stormhaven team — we're currently seeing elevated errors for your production app due to an overload of short-lived outbound connections on the NAT path. We've temporarily shifted egress to a standby gateway and rerouted 80% of traffic through the NLB to reduce failures. Errors have dropped from ~32% to ~2%. We're monitoring closely and will follow up with a full RCA and timeline for a permanent fix. ETA for next update: 30 mins. — Elaine, Redwood Support"

maria: LGTM, send it and include contact for followups.

elaine: sent to customer at 09:31 UTC (ticket #SH-4773).

oncall-bot: @maria you have incident owner role. remember to file postmortem within 72h.

maria: will do. handing incident to luca for long-lived remediation work. luca you're owner now. please add details to the incident ticket and schedule a followup sync with Stormhaven in 48h.

luca: taking ownership. filing ticket INFRA-1229 with remediation options and a migration plan. thanks everyone.

[reaction] :thumbsup: from raj, kai, elaine

maria: summary for postmortem: root cause: conntrack exhaustion on shared NAT caused intermittent TCP resets -> ALB healthchecks failed -> elevated 5xx. mitigation: route shift to standby NAT + SG allowlist + traffic weight shift to NLB reduced errors to acceptable levels. next actions: dedicate egress for tenant or tune conntrack, add runbook step for quick weighted reroute and SG allowlist, add alert for conntrack utilization at 75%.

luca: noted. I'll include timeline, diffs, and rollback steps in INFRA-1229.

elaine: closing loop with customer in the ticket thread, will attach summary and next steps.

maria: incident resolved for now; keeping monitoring for 1h. thanks all.
